title: Why SaaS pricing should start from the price point: avoid the low-price trap and price for results
summary: Tibo argues SaaS founders should work backwards from a price range ($29-$99) rather than use psychological pricing tricks. Low prices signal low quality, and raising Tweet Hunter from $9 to $49 cut conversion slightly but lowered churn and raised LTV. Price for the results delivered to people who badly need them.

principles.text: Work backwards from the price point: pick a price range first, then decide what to build and how.
principles.quote: You work backwards from the price point.

principles.text: Low prices don't attract more customers long-term; they signal low quality, and the planned later price rise never comes.
principles.quote: Here's the truth: Later never comes.

principles.text: High-value customers don't care about price if the product solves a burning problem; a low price can't make up for low value.
principles.quote: A low price DOESN'T compensate for delivering LOW value.

principles.text: Raising prices cuts conversion a little but lowers churn; the LTV bump offset the conversion drop every time at Tweet Hunter.
principles.quote: EVERY SINGLE TIME we raised prices, the LTV bump made for the conversion drop.

principles.text: Complainers about price are often your most reliant users; the real churn is silent cancellations from people who see no value.
principles.quote: People who complain often LOVE your product

principles.text: Price for results, target people who value them, don't fear raising prices, and build premium to charge premium.
